prompt.context: Henry's is a local furniture retail store in Houston, TX. Henry, the owner, has called in BCG because he has seen declining profits in the last few years and would like your help.
prompt.question: How would you advise Henry?

clarifying_info.q: How many locations does Henry's have?
clarifying_info.a: Henry's is a singular store located in a popular shopping area in Houston.
Henry's revenues are through brick and mortar sales only. Henry's does not sell online.

clarifying_info.q: Does Henry's sell products other than furniture?
clarifying_info.a: Henry's does not sell anything outside of furniture.

clarifying_info.q: How does Henry's source its products?
clarifying_info.a: Henry's is a typical retailer. It orders furniture from various manufacturers and distributors throughout the US and sells a variety of popular brands to end customers.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a specific profit target?
clarifying_info.a: There is no specific profit goal or other objectives.

clarifying_info.q: Have revenues been declining as well?
clarifying_info.a: Sales and revenues have not decreased in the last 3 years. The industry is currently strong.

exhibits.shows: Income statement line items for IKEO, a furniture chain that manufactures and sells its own furniture via stores and online, for fiscal year 2015

framework: Profit = Revenue − Costs; diagnose which side is driving declining profits
Revenue: price, volume, product mix, customer segments, channels (brick-and-mortar only)
Cost − Fixed: lease/mortgage, management/fixed labor, overhead/SG&A, marketing/advertising
Cost − Variable: COGS (purchase price from manufacturers/distributors), variable labor (sales force), delivery expenses
External factors: industry health, competitive landscape, macro environment

questions.prompt: Calculate gross profit and operating profit for Henry's in 2015, then interpret the results.
questions.guidance: Candidate computes Gross Profit = Sales − COGS and Operating Profit = Gross Profit − SG&A − Marketing. Should note that operating profit is negative (loss), signaling a structural cost problem.

math.setup: Gross Profit = Sales − COGS; Operating Profit = Gross Profit − SG&A − Marketing/Advertising
math.answer: Henry's gross profit is $195K (≈39% margin); operating profit is $25K (≈5% margin). Profitability is thin and any cost increase could easily push it to a loss.

questions.prompt: Compare Henry's margins to IKEO's margins. What do you notice?
questions.guidance: Because the stores are different sizes, candidate must compare margins (not absolute dollars). Strong response immediately flags the gross margin gap and hypothesizes structural reasons.

math.setup: Gross Margin = (Sales − COGS) / Sales for each company
math.answer: IKEO's gross margin (80%) is roughly double Henry's (39%), suggesting IKEO has a dramatically lower cost base relative to sales — likely because it manufactures its own furniture and sells online, eliminating distributor markups.

questions.prompt: Brainstorm reasons why IKEO's gross margin is so much higher than Henry's.
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate multiple structural reasons across supply chain, channels, and scale.

brainstorming.prompt: Why is IKEO's gross margin so much higher than Henry's? What structural advantages does IKEO have?

categories.name: Supply chain / COGS
ideas: IKEO manufactures its own furniture, eliminating manufacturer and distributor margins (margin stacking)
Henry's pays multiple intermediaries (manufacturer → distributor → retailer), each taking a cut
IKEO benefits from volume-based procurement at scale

categories.name: Sales channel
ideas: IKEO sells online, which has lower overhead per transaction than a physical store
Online sales eliminate store-level variable costs (sales staff commissions, in-store delivery logistics)
Henry's is limited to brick-and-mortar, which has higher operating costs per unit sold

categories.name: Scale
ideas: IKEO's $5M in sales vs. Henry's $495K — larger scale spreads fixed costs and gives negotiating power
Higher volume lowers per-unit logistics and marketing costs for IKEO

categories.name: Brand / product control
ideas: IKEO sells its own branded products with full pricing control; Henry's sells third-party brands where manufacturers set floor prices
Henry's may lack the ability to differentiate on price or product

recommendation: Henry's profitability problem is driven by high COGS relative to sales — a structural cost disadvantage versus vertically integrated, omnichannel competitors like IKEO
Henry can regain profitability, but must address its cost structure: either renegotiate supplier terms, explore alternative lower-cost suppliers, or selectively introduce higher-margin product lines
Launching an e-commerce channel could reduce per-transaction costs but requires significant upfront investment and carries execution risk for a single-store operator
risks: Building an online channel requires capital investment in website, logistics, and fulfillment infrastructure that Henry's may not have
Renegotiating with suppliers risks supply disruption or loss of brand access
The furniture retail market is competitive; IKEO and other large chains have structural advantages that may be difficult to overcome for a single-store retailer
Failure to act quickly may cause further margin erosion as competitors continue to scale
next_steps: Conduct a detailed supplier cost analysis to identify renegotiation opportunities or lower-cost alternatives
Evaluate feasibility and ROI of an online sales channel (build vs. partner vs. marketplace such as Wayfair)
Benchmark SG&A and marketing spend against industry norms to identify additional cost savings
Set a 90-day target to present Henry with a revised cost structure and a 3-year profitability roadmap
